summary: Blame's source lines and the conflict editor's result draft draw in the code font, and the PR review's line-number columns are sized from the code font's digit width at the current code size. With Settings' desktop monospace row on and fontconfig's monospace set to JetBrains Mono: Blame of HEAD's src/cursor.rs, the conflict editor of the same file paused in a merge with its result draft focused, and the offline review fixture's PR #42 Changes rows scrolled to their widest line numbers, in Midnight and Porcelain at interface 13 pt with code 12 and 18 pt, and the review also at code 24 pt; masked base-versus-candidate compares of each, AT-SPI's focused node, and the clearance from each line-number column's ink to the next ink on its row
limitations: Linux under XWayland on GNOME 50 at scale factor 1, display :0, Mutter input; 1000 x 680 for Blame and the review and 1000 x 900 for the conflict editor, whose stack (sides, block actions, a 160 px draft) needs the height. The desktop monospace family is JetBrains Mono through a FONTCONFIG_FILE that prefers it for monospace before including the host's stock /etc/fonts/fonts.conf (warm system cache); it is not the owner's desktop configuration. The fixture is built outside the spec, since a recipe cannot leave a conflicted merge, and opened with --fixture at /tmp/gitturtle-evidence/fixtures/code-font-blame-conflicts-review-gutter/repo: edcd7466 'Add the review cursor', topic 22e1f0ec 'Skip folded lines', HEAD 83de13c1 'Clamp the cursor to the last line', then git merge topic stopped with src/cursor.rs conflicted (UU, stages b8e8a824, 46ad7be2, 662b1dd1); every commit by GitTurtle QA at a fixed 2026-10-05 UTC minute. Blame's source follows the interface size (11 pt scaled), not the code size, in both builds, so its code 18 pt frames show the family only. The offline review fixture's widest line number is 25: two digits fit the 36 px floor at every code size up to 24 pt (2 x 14.4 px in JetBrains Mono at 24 pt), so the candidate's columns equal the base's and no frame can show a number wider than 36 px; that case is the unit test's (five digits at 24 pt). The result draft's caret blinks with a 1 s period; each capture is whichever phase two grabs 1 s apart agreed on, and the compares mask the draft. The ligature switch-off is not shown against a ligature-drawing build: the base draws Blame in DejaVu Sans Mono and the draft in the interface font, neither of which joins characters. macOS, native Wayland, fractional scales, hover, live GitHub and Compare's gutter are not covered

home.fontconfig-qa/fonts.conf:
<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
<!-- The desktop's monospace family for this run: JetBrains Mono, which has programming ligatures, preferred before the host's stock configuration; that configuration and its system cache follow. -->
<fontconfig>
	<alias binding="strong">
		<family>monospace</family>
		<prefer><family>JetBrains Mono</family></prefer>
	</alias>
	<include ignore_missing="no">/etc/fonts/fonts.conf</include>
</fontconfig>
